Claim: For any natural number n, g(n) = 2 - 2/3^n.

Inductive Predicate: let P(n) := g(n) = 2 - 2/3^n.

Base Case I: (n = 0):

g(0) = 0 by the definition of g

g(n) = 2 - 2/3^n when n = 0 evaluates to 2 - 2/3^0 = 2 - 2 = 0

g(1) = 4/3 by the definition of g

g(n) = 2 - 2/3^n when n = 1 evaluates to 2 - 2/3^1 = 2 - 2/3 = 4/3

(Strong) Inductive Hypothesis: Assume for all n = k where k ∈ℕ that P(0), P(1), P(2), ... , P(k) are true.

Inductive Step: We must show that for n = k + 1 that g(k + 1) = 2 - 2/3^k + 1

Considering the left hand side, g(k + 1) = 4/3g(k + 1 - 1) - 1/3g(k + 1 - 2) = 4/3g(k) - 1/3g(k - 1)

= 4/3[2 - 2/3^k] - 1/3[2 - 2/3^k - 1]

= 8/3 - 8/3^k + 1 - 2/3 + 2/3^k

= 8/3 - 2/3 - 8/3^k + 1 + 2/3^k

= 2 - 8/3^k + 1 + 2 * 3/3^k * 3 = 2 - 8/3^k + 1 + 6/3^k + 1

= 2 - 2/3^k + 1

Hence we have shown that P(k + 1) holds.
